solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: African doctor locating set of instruments in Morocco?

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is held inside its outer letters

blocks.note: MA is Morocco's international vehicle registration code
a gang is a set of tools or instruments working together

explanation.surface: A doctor somewhere in Africa tracks down a kit of medical instruments in Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: A gang of tools (as in a gang of saws) is a set used together, which is the sense here rather than a band of people.
explanation.definitionFit: In East Africa an mganga is a traditional healer or witch doctor, so it names a native medical practitioner.

clue.text: Varied firms choose foremost of ungulates producing musk

indicators.note: something varied has been changed about, so the letters come in a different order
the foremost part of a word is the very front, so keep only its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Assorted companies pick the leading hoofed animals that yield musk, as if for the perfume trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FIRMS CHOOSE plus the U of ungulates are rearranged; the musk deer, an ungulate, makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is built from Latin moschus, musk, plus -ferous, bearing, so it describes animals or glands yielding that scent.

clue.text: Neat run out from spinning round

indicators.note: something taken out from a word is removed, leaving the rest behind

blocks.note: gyral means whirling or moving in a circle
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A batsman is run out after a spinning delivery comes round.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat is an old word for cattle, not tidy. Removing the R of GYRAL leaves GYAL, a variant spelling of gayal.
explanation.definitionFit: The gyal or gayal is a domesticated Asian ox, and neat is the old collective word for bovine cattle.

clue.text: Orange colouring matter to curdle unopened oil

indicators.note: with no opening, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: earn is a Scots and dialect verb meaning to curdle milk
otto (attar) is a fragrant oil pressed from roses

explanation.surface: An orange dye is said to make a sealed bottle of oil go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To curdle' sounds like the dye's effect, but it is a rare Scots and dialect verb; 'oil' here is the rose oil of perfumery, not engine oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnotto is a variant of annatto, the orange-red dye from achiote seeds used to tint cheese and butter.

clue.text: Riding horse or ruminant?

blocks.note: a nag is a horse for riding
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is this a horse to ride, or some cud-chewing beast?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface offers a choice of animals; in fact the first two words and the conjunction spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The nagor is a West African reedbuck, an antelope that chews the cud like cattle and deer.

clue.text: Teasmade perhaps as prepared in room

blocks.note: à la, in cookery, means in the style of or as prepared in
RM is the standard abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: A bedside tea maker, the sort set up in a guest room.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teasmade is a British bedside machine that brews tea and has a built-in clock that wakes you; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Teasmade is one kind of wake-up device, since its clock rouses the sleeper as the tea brews.

clue.text: Plastic bullets battery directed towards square

blocks.note: the first three letters of battery, a recognised short form
aimed on something is directed at it
S is the abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: Riot police fire plastic rounds from an artillery battery aimed at a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: Battery reads as artillery, which suits bullets, but it is only the abbreviation BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Baton rounds is the official British term for plastic or rubber bullets used in riot control.

clue.text: Bar recalled uncle Dick leaving $100 on the counter, a trifling amount?

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word runs backwards
what leaves a word goes out of it, so its letter is dropped
counter means contrary, running the opposite way to normal

blocks.note: a pub is a bar
Uncle Dick is Cockney rhyming slang for sick
C is the Roman numeral 100, and a C-note is a hundred-dollar bill

explanation.surface: At the pub, a relative leaves a hundred dollars on the bar, and it is treated as small change.
explanation.walkthrough: PUB is reversed; SICK loses its C and is also reversed. Rhyming slang drops the rhyme: Uncle Dick stands for sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Bupkis is Yiddish-derived American slang for nothing at all, so it fits a trivial or worthless quantity.

clue.text: Ghanaians ground tahina around Sabbath

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed and broken up, so its letters are rearranged
going around something means enclosing it on both sides

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
S is the abbreviation for Sabbath

explanation.surface: People from Ghana grind sesame paste for the day of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Tahina is tahini, the sesame paste; its letters are mixed up with S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashanti are a major ethnic group of central Ghana, once a powerful West African kingdom.

clue.text: Horn players extremely brief, finishing early

indicators.note: stopping before the end means the final letter is never reached

blocks.note: too means excessively, extremely
terse means brief or curt

explanation.surface: Brass players whose piece was far too short, ending ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: TOO TERSE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooter is anyone who toots, sounding a horn or similar wind instrument with short blasts.

clue.text: Prickly shrub, very black, found in corner of Scotland

indicators.note: what is found in a place sits inside it, enclosed

blocks.note: neuk is the Scots word for a corner or nook
BB marks a very soft, very black pencil lead

explanation.surface: A thorny bush with very dark wood grows in a remote part of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corner of Scotland' looks like a place on the map, but it asks for the Scots word for a corner; pencil leads are graded by blackness, with double B very soft and dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebbuk (nabk) is the Christ's-thorn, a spiny Middle Eastern jujube bush.

clue.text: Mineral cast with possible cracking

indicators.note: cracking breaks things apart, letting the letters reassemble

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A mineral specimen moulded, perhaps showing fissures.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast seems a verb for the mineral, but it is just four letters joining POSSIBLE in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Speiss cobalt is an old name for smaltite, a grey cobalt arsenide ore mined as a cobalt source.

clue.text: A lot of alcohol in maize bread accompaniment at wedding?

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the end is cut
one thing set in another is held inside its outer letters

blocks.note: lush is American slang for liquor
pone is a flat bread of maize meal from the southern US

explanation.surface: Plenty of drink is soaked into the cornbread served at a wedding reception.
explanation.walkthrough: Lush usually means a drunkard, but in America it can mean the drink itself. Pone, or corn pone, is a southern US bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus-one is the extra guest an invitee may bring, the partner who comes along to a wedding or party.

clue.text: Buddhist community celebrated in this year

blocks.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it in song
HA is short for Latin hoc anno, in this year

explanation.surface: A group of Buddhists marked an anniversary within the current year.
explanation.walkthrough: Celebrated is taken in the old sense of praised in song, giving a past-tense verb rather than the adjective famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The sangha is the Buddhist order of monks and nuns, and more broadly the whole body of followers.

clue.text: Artemis having eminence in lead role at last

indicators.note: at the last means at the very end, so keep only the final letter
to have something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a hoe is a promontory or projecting height, as in Plymouth Hoe
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: The goddess Artemis is a star taking the leading role at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead role' looks like a theatre part, but lead is the metal; eminence is a raised piece of ground, not fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebe, meaning bright, is a poetic name for the moon goddess Artemis, as Phoebus is for her brother Apollo.

clue.text: What makes this? Pressure on top of cork can

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter
placed on the rest in an across clue, this piece comes after it

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
can is slang for a lavatory, as is loo
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at a corked can under pressure: what made that noise?
explanation.walkthrough: 'What makes this?' asks for the sound itself: the wordplay pictures pressure on a cork, which is how the noise arises. Can and loo are both slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloop is the hollow popping sound of a cork being drawn from a bottle, so it is the noise produced.

clue.text: Sock? Start to iron one in creases all round

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
turning all the way round makes the sequence face backwards

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a batsman standing at the crease in cricket is called a bat

explanation.surface: A sock: start ironing one, and it is creased all over.
explanation.walkthrough: Creases look like folds from ironing, but they are the cricket creases where a batsman stands; a batter is often called a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabi are Japanese ankle socks with a split toe, worn with sandals, so they are a kind of sock.

clue.text: Worthless receding markets in America inhibiting an option for gambling?

indicators.note: something receding moves backwards, so the letters run back
to inhibit is to hold in, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: marts are markets
in, plus US for America
E O, even-odd, is an old gambling game, its name being the two options

explanation.surface: Falling markets in the US, held back by betting, prove worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: E O was an eighteenth-century casino game, a precursor of roulette, named for its even and odd bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Stramineous literally means strawy, and straw is the traditional image of something of no value.

clue.text: Temperature sure to be affected after I caught jaundice

indicators.note: something affected has been altered, so the letters change their order

blocks.note: taken as written
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
T for temperature plus sure, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A patient's temperature is bound to rise once they have caught jaundice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the mixed letters behind I and C; 'caught' looks like catching an illness but is the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Icterus is the medical term for jaundice, the yellowing of skin and eyes from excess bilirubin.

clue.text: One scribbling shortened article about bridge’s opening rubber

indicators.note: a shortened word has lost its end
scribbling is messy, jumbled writing, so the letters are scrambled
the opening of a word is its first letter
lying about something means surrounding it

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
an item is an article, as in a newspaper
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A writer trims a piece about the start of a bridge game played in rubbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One scribbling' reads as a writer, but scribbling is the anagram signal; rubber suggests a game of bridge, yet it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebonite is vulcanite, a hard black vulcanised rubber once used for combs, pipe stems and insulators.

clue.text: Trendy seaside town with pier overlooking Blackpool’s front

indicators.note: to overlook something is to leave it out
the front of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Brighton is a resort town on England's south coast, famous for its pier
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fashionable resort whose pier looks out over the front at Blackpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool is another English seaside resort, so the whole surface is a seafront scene; overlooking means ignoring, not looking down on.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-on is slang for fashionably progressive or up to date in attitudes, close to trendy or hip.

clue.text: Singer that is after solo hit securing No 5 in charts

indicators.note: a hit thing is knocked about, so its letters are disturbed
number five names the fifth letter of the word that follows
to secure is to hold fast, so one piece is held inside another
coming after means placed behind the other part

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the fifth letter of the word
i.e., Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A vocalist follows a solo hit that has reached number five in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Singer is not a vocalist but slang for someone who sings to the police; 'No 5' is not a chart position but a letter position.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoolie, short for stool pigeon, is a police informer, and informers are said to sing.

clue.text: Jazz sax mainly delightful, culture’s unspoilt?

definitions.note: a sentence about a laboratory culture; the answer replaces the adjective unspoilt

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so one letter is lost
to jazz something up is to liven and rework it, so its letters move

blocks.note: the instrument's name without its initial letter
nice means pleasant, delightful

explanation.surface: Saxophone jazz is mostly lovely, and the music scene remains unspoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: Culture looks like the arts, which suits jazz, but it is a culture grown in a lab dish. Here 'mainly' drops the first letter rather than the last.
explanation.definitionFit: An axenic culture is free of all other organisms, uncontaminated by anything but the single species grown.

clue.text: No gentleman, as before, father retorted relating to controversy

indicators.note: to retort is literally to turn back, so the sequence is turned backwards

blocks.note: cit, short for citizen, was an old contemptuous word for a townsman or tradesman
a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A father snaps back that someone is no gentleman, just as he said before, in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' flags a dated word: a cit was a city tradesman, sneered at by the gentry as no gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Eristic comes from Greek eris, strife, and describes argument for its own sake, disputation and wrangling.

clue.text: Scots engaged with short film on tablet

indicators.note: here on means attached to, so the second-named piece is set before the first

blocks.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet
an ident is a short film that identifies a television channel

explanation.surface: Scottish viewers are absorbed by a short film shown on a tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablet' looks like a screen to watch the film on, but it is the drug ecstasy, E; 'Scots' signals a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eident is a Scots adjective meaning diligent, busy and attentive, close to being fully occupied with a task.

clue.text: Earnest planner to go, returning schedule hiding deception

indicators.note: something hiding another keeps it out of sight inside
a thing returning goes back the way it came

blocks.note: to exit is to go out
to cog is to cheat, especially to load dice
a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: A serious organiser is leaving, his timetable reversed to conceal some trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: Cog survives mainly in crosswords, from the old practice of cogging dice to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To excogitate is to think out or devise carefully, so an excogitator is a deep plotter or deviser of schemes.

clue.text: Snickers? Just one bite he eagerly swallows

definitions.note: a single snicker, so a noun in the singular

indicators.note: something swallowed sits inside unseen, lodged within the surrounding text

blocks.note: running across the word boundaries of these three words

explanation.surface: A greedy eater wolfs down a chocolate bar, managing only one bite.
explanation.walkthrough: Snickers looks like the chocolate bar, which suits the bite and swallowing, but it is the plural of a sniggering laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee-hee is a single suppressed giggle, which is exactly what one snicker is.

clue.text: Institute discounted facilities available for hire

indicators.note: something discounted is left out of the count, so it is dropped

blocks.note: the facilities is a polite term for a lavatory
I is the abbreviation for Institute

explanation.surface: An institution offers its premises for rent at a reduced price.
explanation.walkthrough: Discounted looks like a price cut, but it means not counted, so the letter is removed; facilities is the euphemism for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign reading to let shows that a property is available to rent, the British equivalent of for rent.

clue.text: Rare caribou about Indiana

definitions.note: rare marks an uncommon short form of the animal's name

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
IN is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Indiana

explanation.surface: A seldom-seen reindeer turns up somewhere in Indiana.
explanation.walkthrough: Rare looks like it describes an uncommon animal, but it labels the word as rarely used.
explanation.definitionFit: Rein is a rare shortening of reindeer, and caribou is the North American name for the same species.

clue.text: Four bushels — old measurement carried by strong horse …

indicators.note: a load carried by a beast is held within it

blocks.note: a cob is a sturdy, short-legged horse
O is the abbreviation for old
M is the abbreviation for metre, a measurement

explanation.surface: A sturdy horse hauls four bushels, an old unit of measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old measurement' looks like it describes the bushels; it is split into two short abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A coomb (comb) is an old English dry measure for grain equal to four bushels, half a quarter.

clue.text: Tweaks document signed after short time

indicators.note: coming after something sends this piece second, behind the moment

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
DS is the abbreviation for document signed

explanation.surface: Small changes made to a contract just after it has been signed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the moment first, since in a down clue the following piece goes below.
explanation.definitionFit: Mods is the short form of modifications, small adjustments to software, cars or plans.

clue.text: … it’s one working at a factory?

indicators.note: something working is in motion, so these letters are set moving

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Continuing from the horse: it is one that works in a factory, a mill horse perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the strong horse, so 'it's one working' seems to describe a workhorse; the question mark flags the factory as only one example of a site.
explanation.definitionFit: On site means present at the actual place of work, and a factory is one such workplace.

clue.text: Urge hounds over area by previously clear space

indicators.note: placed by something but previously means set just in front of it

blocks.note: a hall is a large open room, an uncluttered space
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: The huntsman urges the hounds across the ground beside a clearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as across but is the cricket over; 'by previously' tells the solver to put the space in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloa is a hunting cry used to encourage hounds in the chase, and as a verb means to shout them on.

clue.text: One chanting, keen on outstanding person heading off

indicators.note: with its head taken off, a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
a oner is a remarkable or unique person

explanation.surface: A singing enthusiast is drawn to a star performer who is just leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Oner is British slang for someone outstanding, one of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to recite in a singing voice or chant, so an intoner is someone reciting that way.

clue.text: Series of clues cracked by one elderly expert

definitions.note: an adjective in the original sense of knowing; it fits as expert describing a person

indicators.note: a thing cracked open by another has that other forced into it

blocks.note: a scent is a trail of clues to follow, as in a false scent
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An aged puzzle expert breaks open a run of crossword clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Series of clues' suggests a crossword, but it is a trail followed by a detective; 'elderly' signals that the word is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Scient is an obsolete adjective meaning knowing or skilful, from Latin sciens, so it fits as learned or skilled.

clue.text: Edgbaston’s most convenient once again to host timeless Test

indicators.note: without time means the letter standing for time is dropped
a host takes a guest in, holding it inside

blocks.note: surface padding: names the Birmingham cricket ground to set the Test match scene
eft is an obsolete adverb meaning again or afterwards
taken as written

explanation.surface: Edgbaston, the Birmingham cricket ground, is the handiest venue to stage another endless Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edgbaston's' only sets the cricket scene. A timeless Test was an old match with no time limit, but here timeless just removes a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Eftest is Shakespeare's word for readiest or quickest, used by Dogberry in Much Ado, hence most convenient in archaic use.
